site.domainNote: Drawphone — telephone-pictionary party game; archive of past game results

view.name: Game result chain
view.description: Result chain of a past game showing the first word, each player's drawing and the guesses that followed.

regions.label: "Results #1" title with presenter instruction and divider
Alternating chain of words (h1) and drawings (452px canvas images) with 'X drew:' / 'Y thought that was:' captions
Grey well: 'You started with: minion and ended up with: hot dog'
'View more results:' vertical list-group of 6 numbered chain buttons, current one disabled
Done and Exit Archive outline buttons
Credit line 'Drawphone by Tanner Krewson' and GitHub link

evidence.note: Vertical stack of buttons; current chain disabled/greyed; clicking '2. slither' swapped the whole content area to Results #2 in place (verified live), URL unchanged

patterns.rationale: Numbered buttons move between results one at a time like numbered pages, but they read more as peer views (tabs); either interpretation is plausible.
The summary is a Bootstrap 'well' container summarizing the chain; it is a bounded summary of one item but not part of a collection overview.

evidence.note: Chain is a fixed, bounded sequence, not a stream

structure.layout: single narrow centered column (~452px) of stacked headings, drawings and controls; no top nav; minimal footer

aesthetics.typography: Pangolin (hand-drawn rounded marker font) used for everything — headings, captions, buttons, footer
aesthetics.typeScale: Pangolin 40px/500 for the guessed words (h1), 32px for 'Results #1', 24px/500 captions (h4), 20px buttons, 16px body/footer; low weight contrast, size carries hierarchy

notes: Bootstrap 3-style page set in Pangolin. Content is user drawings (452px square canvases with thin #ccc border) interleaved with large guessed words — the telephone chain reads top to bottom. Grey well summarises start vs end word. Results switcher is a Bootstrap list-group of buttons with the current one disabled; switching replaces content in place. No colour beyond black/grey and link blue; colour comes only from the players' drawings.
